title: Six-month Niño 3.4 changes had negative third-moment asymmetry in detrended ERSSTv5 indices for 1950-2025
abstract: We tested the direction of fixed-lag temperature changes in monthly NOAA ERSSTv5 indices for 1950-2025. After removal of month effects and a linear trend, six-month Nino 3.4 changes had a normalized raw third moment of -0.507. Its conditional 95% five-year block interval was -0.747 to -0.197. A 98.75% interval for a four-region comparison was -0.811 to -0.103. Large cooling changes thus had more cubic weight than large warming changes. Other region intervals included zero. The main sign remained with three- and seven-year blocks, no trend removal, centered change skewness and a post-result month-variance scaling check. The 1950-1987 interval included zero. The statistic does not measure event duration or prove a physical feedback. Short dependent records, fitted adjustments, source reconstruction error and period choice limit inference. Code, exact source provenance, annual sufficient statistics, main bootstrap draws, a figure and an offline check support reproduction. External monthly source records stay outside the bundle.

display.caption: Six-month change asymmetry in four Nino regions and Nino 3.4 sensitivity checks. Dark lines show pointwise 95% block intervals. Light lines show 98.75% intervals for the four-region comparison. Negative values give greater cubic weight to cooling changes.
